set.st: James H. Webster, an Indiana man who went to the California gold rush in 1852, settled on a farm near Steamboat Rock in 1876. In May 1897 the Steamboat Rock Echo reported that he distrusted banks, had buried about $1,000 of pension money and several hundred dollars more, and then forgot the spot; searching failed. Wire copies that spring inflated it to $50,000 in casks. He was judged insane that spring and died in the state hospital at Independence in August 1897, leaving several thousand dollars of property. A dowser wrote to the probate judge offering to find his money. No dig find was reported. An Eldora dispatch of 5 June 1897 reported that Webster, by then insane, was taken to jail and that four tin cans holding about $2,000 in gold were found on him, which would cover the local paper's estimate of what he had buried. The estate went intestate in Aug 1897 on a $6,000 bond, which points to about $3,000 of personal property expected, not $50,000.
set.t: The local amount (about $1,000-1,500) is the believable one, and $2,000 in gold was found on him in June 1897, so little if anything is likely still in the ground. One local source (the editor 'can not vouch'); his obituary adds that he was said to carry considerable money on his person, which may mean some of it was never buried. Place Webster's farm in Clay Township on an 1890s Hardin plat. Access: private: permission.
set.tovw: Lead grade D: the June 1897 report of $2,000 in gold found on him accounts for the local $1,000-1,500 said to be buried; only the inflated wire figure of $50,000 leaves anything to seek

src: Audubon Republican (Audubon, Iowa), 10 Jun 1897, p. 4, 'Miser's Gold Is Found', Eldora dispatch of 5 Jun 1897 (Chronicling America sn87057928/1897-06-10/ed-1/?sp=4)
